describes: Modal-head phrases the prose grammar's modal_head production recognises, each mapped to one of the three canonical lexemes (shall/must/may) the truth table (_NEGATED_MODAL in deontic.prose_grammar) dispatches on. A data table, not a regex: the recursive-descent parser matches a phrase's words at a token position; it does not compile or search a pattern. Multi-word phrases are tried longest-first at each position. An entry may also carry a literal 'operator' (F only, Phase 1 scope): the phrase itself already lexicalises a negated modal ('is prohibited from', 'is not permitted to'), so the grammar dispatches straight to that operator instead of through the lexeme/negation table. English only (Phase 1 scope).
